episode_title: Howard Hochhauser on Purpose-Driven Leadership, AI-Powered Growth, and the Power of Storytelling

real_qa.q: What is Ancestry.com's most important KPI and why is it called time to magic?
real_qa.r: Ancestry.com's primary KPI is time to magic, defined as the time from when a customer signs up for a family history subscription until they experience a heart-touching, emotional moment—measured within the free trial window of two weeks. Howard Hochhauser explains that magic is giving somebody a story that moves them, making them laugh or cry, and compelling them to share it with others. The goal is to accelerate time to magic by creating personalized, curated audio and video stories about ancestors using AI-digitized records and family photos.

real_qa.q: How is Ancestry.com using AI to create personalized family stories for customers?
real_qa.r: Ancestry.com uses AI primarily in the backend to digitize and bring more content to subscribers rather than as a standalone widget. The company is combining employment records, draft cards, service files and other ancestor records with AI to automatically create personalized stories; these stories can include customer-uploaded photos or company-digitized images. The vision is to create 30-second and 60-second highly personalized audio and video stories about customers and their families—an impossible task before AI—with video storytelling becoming viable once costs decrease.

real_qa.q: What was Ancestry.com's mission statement before Howard Hochhauser became CEO, and why did he change it?
real_qa.r: The previous mission was we empower journeys of personal discovery, which Hochhauser felt was too elastic and unfocused—so broad it could apply to a yoga studio or health clinic. Upon becoming CEO, he changed the mission to discover, preserve, and share your family history, family stories. He explains that this new mission immediately attracted employees passionate about finding specific records like draft cards or railroad service records that reveal who their ancestors truly were, and the change refocused the entire company on what it actually does.

real_qa.q: What was Ancestry.com's financial and customer satisfaction situation when Howard Hochhauser became CEO, and how did he turn it around?
real_qa.r: When Hochhauser took over as CEO, the company was not performing well financially, had experienced a series of layoffs, revenue was declining, and customer satisfaction was declining. He achieved eight consecutive quarters of growth by focusing entirely on growth and product improvement, hiring a new CFO to handle finance, updating the mission and culture statement to the three Cs (Customers, Candid, Collaborative), and emphasizing focus on customer needs. He established his leadership authentically through personal storytelling in his first company presentation, which helped unite employees around shared purpose.
real_qa.requete: Ancestry.com financial turnaround eight quarters growth

real_qa.q: How does Ancestry.com balance privacy and customer trust with DNA data, especially following 23andMe's security issues?
real_qa.r: Ancestry.com places privacy and customer trust at the center of everything, with the principle that customer data—whether photos or DNA tests—belongs to the customer who controls what they do with it. Hochhauser says he would never want to surprise his mother with something Ancestry is doing, ensuring all actions pass that customer-centric test. Following 23andMe's security breaches, Ancestry was ahead on technology initiatives including multi-factor authentication that 23andMe and others did not have, and conducts regular tabletop exercises and postmortems to stay on top of data privacy and security.

guest.bio_context: Howard Hochhauser has spent 18 years at Ancestry.com, starting as CFO before moving to Chief Operating Officer and becoming CEO approximately two years before this interview. Prior to Ancestry, he was CFO at Martha Stewart. He relocated from New York to Utah driven by passion for the company's mission of helping people discover their family histories and preserve their stories.

real_quote: Our customers love solving problems, they love making discoveries, they love seeing more content come from Ancestry—and we're using AI in the back end to bring more content to subscribers.
